prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing / editorial software illustration.
Create ONE polished wide landscape illustration for the ShardPilot open-source project's documentation, approximately 3:2 landscape, with beautifully legible English typography. This is a new composition; the supplied avatar is a STYLE AND BRAND IDENTITY REFERENCE ONLY, not a canvas to edit.
MESSAGE: ShardPilot is a recommended companion for agent orchestration environments where many coding agents rapidly add tests and the growing suite benefits from intelligent, duration-aware class-level sharding in CI.
Use the exact Grinnotech Platform visual language of the reference: deep forest green #063D26 background, lime #A0EF3B top faces, green #388E24 side faces, pale mint #CDFFD8 symbols and base planes; clean precise isometric cubic architecture, restrained dimensional shading, premium technical editorial design. No blue, orange or purple. No photo realism. Strong spacing and visual hierarchy, generous safe margins.
At the top, large headline in pale mint, exactly:
"More agents. More tests."
Below it, large lime headline, exactly:
"Balanced CI with ShardPilot."
Below the headline, an elegant small outlined pill with a simple check symbol and the exact wording:
"Recommended for agent orchestration"
This is the project's own recommendation; do not add external certification, customer logos, scores, or badges from other companies.
The lower two thirds tell one clear LEFT-TO-RIGHT story, as a coherent isometric scene:
LEFT: an orchestration hub (network of nodes) connects to three small friendly abstract coding-agent modules, each with a subtle terminal/code glyph. They produce a growing flow of MANY individual mint test cards, with code/check symbols, forming an increasingly large queue of test classes. Agents are generic, not vendor-branded. Increasing abundance reads as test-suite growth, not errors.
CENTER: a large handsome green ShardPilot control module bearing the recognizable mint three-way fan-out symbol from the avatar: one incoming stem splitting into three upward/diagonal outward arrows. It receives the queue and distributes test CLASS cards to three parallel CI execution lanes. The word "ShardPilot" is written clearly on its base.
RIGHT: three distinct parallel execution lanes on separate green isometric trays, populated by differently sized test-class blocks. Their total lengths are visually comparable to convey balancing by historical test duration, without claiming mathematically identical loads. Each lane ends with a small mint successful check on its own worker cube. Exactly three lanes, no fourth implied lane. These illustrate configurable shard counts rather than a product limit.
Use visible thin directional connectors from agents to test queue to ShardPilot to lanes. Make the entire flow unambiguous and keep the central fan-out mark recognizable. Include ONLY three small stage labels aligned neatly underneath their respective stages:
"Agent teams"     "Growing test suite"     "Duration-aware shards"
The branded module name, pill and the above exact headline/stage labels are the only text. No tiny invented code, no percentages, no time-savings numbers, no speedometer. No implying ShardPilot orchestrates the agents or launches CI workers: the agents are upstream; the output lanes are CI-owned independent executions. No vendor/framework/database logos are needed in this illustration. No embedded UI screenshot, no border, no cropped objects.
Beautiful editorial balance, high clarity at README width, green-on-mint geometric craftsmanship matching the reference.
notes: Project-authored recommendation, not a third-party endorsement.
Three lanes illustrate configurable shard counts; historical timings guide class assignment, while CI launches executions.
The style reference was an earlier ecosystem concept, withdrawn from publication; the final illustration uses generic symbols without third-party product logos.
